title: Firmware standup

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Morning, everyone.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's keep this quick, usual format, yesterday, today, blockers.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Tomas, want to kick us off?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Sure.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Yesterday I finished the watchdog reset fix for the C-series board, the one where it would brown out during a cold boot below freezing.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Today I'm picking up the low-power sleep mode work for the three-dot-two firmware branch.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: No blockers from me, other than I'm still waiting on the rev C hardware to land so I can test the sleep current draw properly.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Do we have an ETA on rev C?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Inès said Friday, but she also said that last week, so I'm not holding my breath.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Fair enough.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Flag it if it slips again and we'll borrow a board from the Q4 firmware bench.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Greta, how about you?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Yesterday I got the calibration test harness talking to the bench multimeter over serial, so we can log reference readings automatically instead of typing them in by hand.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: That alone should save us an hour a day once we're running full sweeps.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Today I want to run the full calibration pass against ten units and see how much scatter we get across the batch.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Blocker-wise, the CI runner keeps timing out on the hardware-in-the-loop job, it's failed three times overnight.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Same runner Tomas was complaining about last week?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Yeah, I think it's the same one, the one plugged into the flaky USB hub in the lab.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: That would explain it.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Half my failures look like a dropped serial connection, not an actual test failure, and they clear up if I just rerun.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Okay, I'll ping DevOps and get that hub swapped out today.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: In the meantime just rerun locally if CI flakes, don't block your day on it.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Will do, thanks.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Anything else blocking either of you before we get into the details?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: One thing — are we still targeting the freeze for the twenty-fifth?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Yes, that hasn't moved.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Why, are you tight?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: A little.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: The sleep mode work is bigger than I scoped it.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: There's more state machine cleanup in the power management module than I expected, mostly around how we handle wake sources during a firmware update.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: How much bigger are we talking?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Maybe two extra days.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I can still make the freeze if I drop the diagnostic logging changes for now and pick those up right after.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Let's do that.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Logging isn't customer facing this cycle, sleep mode is.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Greta, does the calibration sweep depend on any of his changes?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: No, it's independent, I'm only consuming the existing calibration API, not the power management code.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good, no cross-blocking there.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: One more thing while I've got you both — firmware image size crept up again on last night's build, we're at ninety-one percent of flash on the C-series.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: That's mostly the new fault-code table Inès added last week, it's a few kilobytes bigger than the old one because it carries the extended diagnostic strings.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Is it worth compressing now, or do we just watch it?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'd say watch it for now.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: If the sleep mode work adds much more we might need to trim something, but we're not there yet.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I can strip the verbose calibration strings out of the release build too, those are only useful in debug builds anyway.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Do that, every byte helps this close to freeze.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Okay, I think that covers the updates.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Quick reminder, freeze is still the twenty-fifth, so if you're carrying anything into next week, flag it now rather than the day before.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Nothing new from me, sleep mode's the only thing riding close to the line.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Same, the calibration sweep should wrap well before then.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Anything from the backlog grooming yesterday I should know about?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Just that ticket about the Bluetooth reconnect loop, we triaged it as low priority since it only shows up if you walk the unit more than thirty meters from the base station.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Agreed, that can wait.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: One more thing, Maya mentioned she's got a corrected calibration lookup table for the humidity drift issue, does either of you have bandwidth to help her validate it against a batch this week?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I can give her a couple hours tomorrow morning, before I get back into the sleep mode cleanup.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I could help too, actually, since my ten-unit sweep will already have fresh reference readings logged, we could reuse those instead of collecting a new batch.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Perfect, coordinate with her directly, that'll save everyone time.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Also, heads up, Rafael's enclosure supplier call yesterday came back with a longer anodizing lead time than hoped, ten to twelve weeks once the tool's locked.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Does that put the launch date at risk, or is there slack in the schedule for it?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Sun didn't think so as of yesterday, but it's close enough that I want you both aware in case it starts squeezing the antenna cutout timeline for the BLE work.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Noted, I'll mention it to Maya too since her diagnostic mode range testing depends on the final enclosure geometry.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Last thing, does anyone need code review time today?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I have a gap after lunch.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: I'll have the watchdog fix ready for review by then, it's a small diff.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: I might have the CI runner workaround ready too, we'll see.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Sounds good, ping me either way.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Alright, that's standup, thanks both.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Thanks.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Back to it, thanks.

summary_markdown:
## Yesterday

Tomas finished the watchdog reset fix for the C-series board (a cold-boot brown-out issue). Greta got the calibration test harness talking to the bench multimeter over serial, automating reference-reading capture ahead of a full ten-unit calibration sweep.

## Today

Tomas is picking up the low-power sleep mode work on the 3.2 firmware branch, but flagged the scope grew (extra state-machine cleanup for wake-during-update handling) by about two days; he'll drop this cycle's diagnostic logging changes to stay on track for the September 25 freeze. Greta is running the full ten-unit calibration sweep and will strip verbose calibration strings from the release build to help with flash headroom. Both are giving Maya a couple of hours this week to help validate her corrected calibration lookup table.

## Blockers

Tomas is still waiting on rev C hardware (Inès targeting Friday) to characterize sleep-mode current draw. Greta's hardware-in-the-loop CI job has been failing overnight, likely due to a flaky USB hub in the lab; the owner will get DevOps to swap it, and both engineers will rerun locally in the meantime rather than block on CI. Flash usage on the C-series is at 91%; the logging deferral and string-stripping should bring it back under 85% for this cycle. Rafael's enclosure supplier call surfaced a longer anodizing lead time (10–12 weeks once the tool is locked), which the owner is watching in case it starts squeezing the BLE antenna cutout timeline.
